topics.flagship-ru-ua: Humanitarian evacuation reportedly began from besieged Oleshky, as Russia and Ukraine observed what four outlets called the most significant truce of the war. Elsewhere, Russian strikes caused major power outages in Dnipro, and a reported Ukrainian drone attack started a fire at a Russian oil refinery. Other items include a rising death toll in Izium (five), Novaya Gazeta shutting down under official pressure, a Russian arrested in Poland for photographing railways, and Russian claims that Ukraine killed a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant welder. Each of these is carried by one outlet only.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Two outlets report an Israeli siege of Hebron through 10 entrances, with about 5,000 people forced to flee. Israeli strikes continue in Gaza despite the ceasefire, and Gaza's Health Ministry is urging Rafah to open. On Iran, Qatari mediators returned to Tehran to push a US-Iran deal while Trump keeps threats on the table, saying the war will "get wrapped up soon" and that he needs a guarantee Tehran will never get nuclear weapons. Separately, a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly hit by limpet mines, the first successful use of such explosives in the waterway since the US-Iran war began. Oil markets are caught between war risk and emergency SPR releases, and a Hudson Institute report details alleged Iranian plots in Britain and other antisemitism-linked security threats.
topics.T15: Coverage is sparse and mixed, with single-outlet items of uneven relevance. Reported events include repeated unusually high tides flooding parts of the California coast, a partial ceiling collapse at an Indian cancer ward during Cyclone Arnab rains (about 12 patients evacuated, no injuries), and a Level 3 alert and six-kilometer evacuation zone after a Mayon volcano eruption in the Philippines. A Hurricane Milton item appears to be older material, and a honeymoon travel piece is generic.
topics.T01: Coverage is fragmented. One outlet reports Houthi shelling and sniper fire in Taiz, Yemen, killing a woman and injuring five civilians. Pakistan's army reportedly destroyed Afghan Taliban posts near South Waziristan and Parachinar in retaliation for shelling. The rest is commentary or diplomatic news, including Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov's presence at a G20 meeting that upset counterparts.
topics.T02: Two outlets report drone strikes on the Jari Number Two displacement camp in South Wollo, Ethiopia, killing at least 18 and prompting mass displacement. More than 28 million people in the DRC face deepening hunger from conflict, Ebola and climate shocks. Other reports describe Ethiopians fleeing into Kenya from Moyale amid gunfire, and Houthis holding 37 UN World Food Programme workers according to the new WFP chief.
topics.T03: Two outlets report allegations that Houthi forces may have used chemical weapons in Taiz, Yemen, based on accounts of civilians struggling to breathe and losing consciousness after artillery and rocket attacks. Calls for an independent international investigation have followed. The use is unverified.
topics.T04: Reporting indicates a major Ebola epidemic in the DRC, reportedly 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths, with 31 cases outside the country; this comes from one outlet. Kenya expects to discharge 46 Ebola contacts from quarantine on November 3. Several other items are old COVID-era articles or academic or generic pieces and are not meaningful for today.
topics.T05: Stories are scattered and single-sourced. A Bangladesh court sentenced a senior Sheikh Hasina ally to death over 2024 uprising killings. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado reportedly returned home intending to push for elections, and another opposition figure reportedly fled to Spain. Flavio Bolsonaro is reportedly in Florida after fleeing Brazil, and exile-community debate over Cuba is also noted. No clear coup indicators appear.
topics.T06: Youth-driven and cost-of-living protests are reported across Europe, with France the focus: a 'very high' risk of disorder is forecast over the Halloween weekend, with about 70,000 police deployed. Italy has nationwide student and union protests, and the Dutch interior minister warned of 'alarming' reports of planned Gen Z riots in several cities. Some coverage is partisan or opinion, including a White House statement citing the French unrest and claims of billionaire funding.
topics.T07: Coverage is too sparse to summarize meaningfully: one RT piece disputes a RUSI report on the future of Russia's strategic nuclear forces.
topics.T08: Five outlets report that a 22-year-old Perth man was charged with allegedly preparing a terrorist attack after arrest by WA's Joint Counter Terrorism Team. Other items are single-source: Nigerian troops repelled an ambush in Kaduna and killed three attackers, killings in Taraba prompted calls for better intelligence, and Nigeria is reviewing its 2019 security strategy. Pakistan reports shooting down five armed drones at a Kharan checkpost, and a church attack in Karak, Jordan, is discussed.
topics.T09: One outlet reports that Trump appeared to link Russia's release of American hostage Stephen Hubbard to his decision to suspend economic sanctions on Moscow. Hubbard met Trump at the Oval Office on Friday.
topics.T10: Two outlets report that Kim Jong Un attended North Korea's first drone exhibition, with over 30 aircraft types, and called for rapidly expanding drone technology. Single-source items include Ethiopia's reported acquisition of 12 Russian Su-35 fighters, India's $22 billion military spending approval, Hegseth proposing a US-ASEAN defense framework in the Philippines, and the US Army reportedly practicing mass-grave procedures for large-scale war. The rest is commentary and tech-sector pieces.
topics.T11: Several exercises are announced or underway. Egypt and Turkey plan a naval exercise for 4–9 November, and the US, Australia, India and Japan hold Malabar 2026 near Japan on 5–12 November. INS Sahyadri began the sea phase of an India-South Korea exercise. A Chinese outlet criticizes Keen Sword 2027, and three Uruguayan soldiers drowned during an exercise.
topics.T12: Ten outlets report that the world's largest crypto exchange, Binance, disclosed approximately $6.3 billion 'impacted' in an apparent hack, and blockchain intelligence firms link it to North Korea. Other reports say hackers disrupted refrigeration systems in hundreds of French supermarkets, and the Pentagon is investigating August freezer failures at US bases as a suspected hack (two sources). Also reported: a breach exposing data on 41,000 DHS employees, an FBI domain seizure of the bulletproof host Virtualine, a ransomware attack on a school district, and a hospital hack claim that included an apology.
topics.T13: Coverage is mostly UK-focused and single-source. Items include a migrant threatening a smuggler with a knife before a Channel crossing, more than 200 unaccompanied children arriving at Dover each month, local opposition to a planned asylum camp in Suffolk, and a possible watering-down of Home Secretary Mahmood's residency rules. Other reports cover Texas deportation politics ahead of the midterms and five HIV cases confirmed among migrants in Ceuta, from a partisan outlet.
topics.T14: One outlet reports that Cuba staged a welcome for Richard Tur, a Cuban UN delegation member expelled from the US after attacking the spokesman of US UN Ambassador Mike Waltz. No other embassy threats are reported.
topics.T16: Final results show Netanyahu's bloc lost its Knesset majority, winning 53 seats against 48 for the main opposition, and Arab-led parties won a historic 19 seats, so coalition talks will be difficult. Germany is cautious on the result. Pope Leo XIV reportedly became the first pope to vote in a US general election, via mail-in ballot. US midterm coverage focuses on the economy, Michigan Senate race tensions, and election-interference concerns, with some partisan commentary.

bluf: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to an apparent hack of Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, which reported roughly $6.3 billion 'impacted'; the claim is carried by 10 outlets and attribution rests on the firms' analysis. Two outlets report that Israel has choked off Hebron at 10 entrances, forcing about 5,000 people to flee. A humanitarian mission reportedly began evacuating the besieged Ukrainian city of Oleshky as Russia and Ukraine observed what four outlets call the most significant truce of the war. Five outlets report that a 22-year-old Perth man was charged with allegedly preparing a terrorist attack after arrest by WA's Joint Counter Terrorism Team. In Israel, final results show Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats against 48 for the main opposition, losing its majority, while Arab-led parties won a historic 19 seats; coalition negotiations will be difficult. Separately, two outlets report limpet mines disabled a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, the first successful use of such explosives there since the US-Iran war began. Qatar is mediating a US-Iran deal even as Trump keeps threats on the table. Two outlets also report suspected chemical weapons use by Houthi forces in Taiz, Yemen, with calls for an international investigation; this is unverified.
